A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same collaborative-inference partitioning study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments across vision models, partition depths, label-smoothing conditions, attack enhancements and auxiliary datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds ResNet-50 experiments, MNIST-target results, automatic partition-zone localization checks and deployment measurements.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an automatic GPZ selection procedure absent from v1. Appendix D and Algorithm 1 compute class-wise radii, normalize by representation dimension, and use relative drops and a threshold to select the transition zone. This adds an operational partition-selection method; the existing feature-enhancement and inversion architectures are largely retained.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix H.7 and Table 10 add MNIST as a reconstruction target, using MNIST, EMNIST and KMNIST as auxiliary sources. In v1, MNIST appears only as auxiliary data for the Japanese-character target. The other target domains remain, and clarifying that KMNIST denotes Kuzushiji-49 does not establish a new dataset.

E2.justification: The attack comparator sets are retained: v1 Tables 3–5 correspond to v3 Tables 9, 3 and 4. The limited addition is Table 5's explicit comparison of the new automatic locator against empirically identified transition zones.

E3.justification: v3 adds SSIM and AlexNet-based LPIPS to MSE/PSNR evaluation, introduces ResNet-50 target configurations, and evaluates automatic localization. Appendix I adds a separate deployment protocol using batch-one inference, eight CPU threads, latency, memory, communication and RAPL energy measurements. The previously stated core dataset splits and optimizer settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test dimension normalization and sampling, training-seed and label-smoothing stability of GPZ localization in Appendix D. Appendix H.5 adds ResNet-50 evidence separating depth from dimensional expansion, H.7 extends auxiliary-distribution analysis to an MNIST target, and Appendix I quantifies deployment trade-offs. The earlier attack-enhancement ablations remain.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports localization agreement across resampled evaluations (3/3, pairwise Jaccard 1.00) and consistency across independent training seeds, although the training-run count is unspecified. Appendix I reports mean/p95 latency over 200 timed passes and a 500-iteration energy window. These are limited additions, not evidence of increased replication for the retained attack results.

E6.justification: The MSE/PSNR values in v1 Tables 3–5 are retained in their corresponding v3 tables. Substantial new results include SSIM/LPIPS scores, ResNet-50 reconstruction outcomes, MNIST-target results, localization comparisons and deployment costs. For example, Table 11 newly reports VGG depth-26/30 mean latencies of 2.60/2.65 ms and payloads of 256/128 KB; these are added measurements, not before-to-after performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's purported entropy-gap bound becomes an explicitly defined gap between upper-bound surrogates in v3 Eq. 8. Eq. 9 adds label-entropy and finite-precision corrections, supported by new discretization/KL derivations in Appendices B–C. Appendices E–F correct label-smoothing normalization, revise gradient-alignment reasoning, add target-reshaping derivations, and replace the unconditional nonzero-gradient claim with bounds requiring overconfidence and suitable Jacobian projections.

C1.justification: v3 elevates active R2-based GPZ localization and label-distribution-controlled training dynamics, termed Neural Vortex, into central contributions. It strengthens the transition claim to necessity for intrinsic resistance while describing the entropy increase through a lower bound. v1 primarily emphasizes favorable transition/decision splits and depth insufficiency. The headline fourfold-MSE and 66% resistance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 revises the account of one-hot radius dynamics and qualifies sustained label-smoothing gradients as an overconfidence phenomenon that vanishes at the smoothed optimum. Appendix C acknowledges potentially vacuous absolute bounds. The discussion adds substantive deployment trade-offs, adverse-distribution limitations and cautious hypotheses for text Transformers; Appendix G explicitly limits Neural Vortex to an explanatory metaphor.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the code placeholder with a concrete repository URL and supplies locator pseudocode, detailed enhancement-module definitions, the CIFAR-10 super-resolution source, and the actual FaceScrub acquisition count of 43,149 images. It also documents preprocessing, LPIPS configuration and deployment measurement procedures. These disclosures do not establish that the retained experiments changed preprocessing or were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with neural collapse, mutual-information regularization and estimation, and encrypted private inference, including Split HE and PRISM. The introduction and Appendix J explicitly frame intrinsic split selection as complementary to existing defenses and distinguish its evaluation from defense-versus-defense competition.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, theoretical narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten around GPZ localization and Neural Vortex. Related work, dataset descriptions, implementation material and face-result discussion move into reorganized appendices with a roadmap. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 4–5 gain SSIM/LPIPS panels, and new localization, ResNet-50, MNIST and deployment displays are introduced. Existing final-output and face results are relocated, with the final-output table expanded and its misleading caption corrected. The document also changes its template and uses full-width appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important weaknesses in v1's entropy-gap reasoning and unconditional label-smoothing gradient claim, and makes partition selection operational through a documented, evaluated locator. Perceptual metrics, implementation disclosures and measured deployment trade-offs substantially strengthen the paper's assessability and practical relevance. Broad necessity claims and some inconsistent gradient wording remain, but these residual weaknesses do not outweigh the theoretical corrections and stronger supporting evidence.
